title: Date Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Date Calculator: Add or subtract days, weeks, months or years. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Date Calculator](/date-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Add or subtract days, weeks, months or years. Enter your start date, operation, years, months, weeks and days and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Find the date that falls a given number of days, weeks, months or years before or after another date — perfect for deadlines, warranties and contracts. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Date & Time tools include [Age Calculator](/age-calculator), [Days Between Dates Calculator](/days-between-dates-calculator) and [Time Calculator](/time-calculator).

## How to use the Date Calculator

Start by picking your start date, then choosing your operation from the list, entering your years, entering your months, entering your weeks and finally entering your days. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Pick your start date.
2. Choose your operation from the list.
3. Enter your years.
4. Enter your months.
5. Enter your weeks.
6. Enter your days.

## Formula

Years and months are applied on the calendar first, then weeks and days are added.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Date Calculator](/date-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 90 days after 1 January 2026 is Thursday, 2 April 2026. Try the same figures in the [Date Calculator](/date-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Start date: today, Operation: Add, Years: 0, Months: 0, Weeks: 0, Days: 90), the [Date Calculator](/date-calculator) returns Resulting date: Fri, February 19, 2027. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Age Calculator](/age-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Adding a month to 31 January rolls into March in short months.
- Use 'Subtract' to find a start date from a deadline.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What date is 30 days from today?

Leave the start date as today and enter 30 days. Try it with your own numbers in the [Date Calculator](/date-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does it handle leap years?

Yes — it uses real calendar arithmetic. Try it with your own numbers in the [Date Calculator](/date-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Date Calculator use?

Years and months are applied on the calendar first, then weeks and days are added. You can see it in action in the [Date Calculator](/date-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Date Calculator?

Just Start date, Operation, Years, Months, Weeks and Days. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
